extension_region.rule: A deployment may stamp any attribute onto the root `chat` span except keys under a reserved prefix and keys this schema already declares on any span. Reserved keys are dropped, not stamped: a deployment that redefined `bitrouter.*` would make the schema deployment-dependent, which is the one thing it exists not to be.
extension_region.value_types: Scalars only — string, bool, integer, float. Null and nested JSON are skipped, because an OTel attribute value is scalar.
extension_region.diagnostic: One DEBUG line per dropped key on the `bitrouter::observe::span_attributes` target.

invariants.rule: Only the root `chat` INTERNAL span carries `gen_ai.*` attributes. The auxiliary spans — `route`, the per-hop CLIENT spans, `settle` — carry `bitrouter.*` and `server.*` only.
invariants.failure: A gen_ai-aware backend renders any span carrying `gen_ai.*` as its own generation. Stamping a hop makes it count two generations per request and double the reported cost. Nothing errors; the bill is just wrong.

invariants.rule: ACP agent spans never carry `gen_ai.usage.*`. Context-window occupancy rides `bitrouter.context.used` / `bitrouter.context.size` instead.
invariants.failure: The substrate reports occupancy, not per-turn deltas. Writing occupancy into the token attributes corrupts every token dashboard built on them, and the numbers look plausible.

invariants.rule: `gen_ai.response.id` carries the gateway-observable id. Under the Responses protocol that is an encoded gateway continuation id; the native upstream id never reaches an exported span.
invariants.failure: A leaked native id is not resolvable through the gateway, so continuation breaks for anyone who reads it off a trace.

invariants.rule: `gen_ai.client.token.usage` is a single histogram; input versus output is the `gen_ai.token.type` dimension.
invariants.failure: Registering a second same-named instrument is a duplicate-instrument conflict: the SDK warns once and merges them anyway, so the split silently does nothing.

invariants.rule: Cardinality caps apply to metric dimensions only. Spans carry raw `api_key_id` / `user_id` values.
invariants.failure: Capping span attributes trades per-tenant debug fidelity for storage the tracing backend was never going to charge for. Cardinality is a metrics concern.

invariants.rule: The scope name, the meter name, and the instrument names are wire contract.
invariants.failure: Dashboards and collector routing rules select on them. Renaming one to track the crate that happens to host the code breaks every consumer, and the export keeps succeeding.
